title: Mirabel and the Trail
premise: Ada Voss, a bush pilot hauling medicine and rumors into the coastal interior, is grounded by debt when the lowest tide in a decade exposes a sea cave her late father's compass seems to point toward — and inside it, the wreck of the Meridian, a salvage legend everyone thought was myth. When a rival salvage fleet catches wind, Ada and her reluctant crew of locals have six tides to reach the wreck first, forcing her to choose between the loyalty she owes the people who kept her flying and the truth about what really sank the Meridian — a truth that implicates her father. The race ends at the sixth tide, where Ada sacrifices the wreck's gold to expose the fleet captain's fraud, clearing her father's name but losing the fortune that would have freed her.
about_author: Edmund Vasquez is the pen name of a former floatplane mechanic who spent nine years ferrying supplies along remote coastlines before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels from a converted boathouse, drawing on the tides, wrecks, and stubborn pilots he came to know.

chapters.title: Cargo and Rumors
chapters.summary: Ada Voss flies medicine into a fog-bound inlet, eavesdropping on gossip about a legendary wreck while dodging her creditors' calls. Her POV establishes her debt, her dead father's tarnished name, and the compass she wears like an apology. Emotional beat: restless unease beneath competent routine.

chapters.title: The Lowest Tide
chapters.summary: Ada's POV: an anomalous tide drains the bay below her strip, revealing a cave mouth her compass needle swings toward like it's called home. She explores briefly, finding carved initials matching her father's. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as she realizes someone else has been watching the water too.

chapters.title: Debt Collectors
chapters.summary: The harbor master, Ruth Okafor (POV), warns Ada that the Corvus salvage fleet has chartered every boat in port and its captain, Silas Crane, is asking about her father. Ruth offers Ada her old skiff if Ada will let the town in on whatever she finds. Emotional beat: loyalty offered before it's tested.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Ada's POV: tide tables confirm the cave will be accessible only six more times before the season closes. She assembles a crew — Ruth, diver Teo Marsh, and her estranged cousin Junie Voss — each carrying their own reason to need the Meridian. Emotional beat: fragile alliance formed out of desperation.

chapters.title: What Junie Knows
chapters.summary: Junie's POV: she reveals letters suggesting their father didn't sink the Meridian by negligence — he was paid to move it, or hide it. Ada refuses to believe it, fracturing the cousins' reunion. Emotional beat: truth arriving too early, before anyone wants it.

chapters.title: First Tide: The Throat
chapters.summary: Ada's POV: the crew runs the cave entrance on the first tide, nearly losing the skiff to a surge channel. Inside they find the Meridian's mast, not the hull — the wreck was moved. Emotional beat: exhilaration undercut by the sense of being led somewhere.

chapters.title: Crane Makes Contact
chapters.summary: Silas Crane's POV: he boards Ada's floatplane at a fuel dock, courteous and menacing, offering to buy her father's compass because 'it belongs with the rest of his mistakes.' Ada declines. Emotional beat: the reader sees Crane knows far more than he should.

chapters.title: Second Tide: Dead Reckoning
chapters.summary: Teo's POV: a dive beyond the mast finds a sealed strongroom, but Teo surfaces with decompression sickness and a salvaged logbook page bearing Ada's father's signature. Emotional beat: the cost of ambition paid in flesh.

chapters.title: The Logbook Page
chapters.summary: Ada's POV: the page suggests her father scuttled the Meridian deliberately to keep its cargo from Crane's predecessor — a privateer's descendant running the same fleet. Loyalty to his memory wars with the evidence. Emotional beat: grief reorganized into purpose.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV: someone cuts the skiff's fuel line overnight; suspicion falls on Junie, who was seen near the dock. Ada defends her cousin against the town's judgment, deepening her own isolation. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen publicly, at a price.

chapters.title: Third Tide: The Strongroom
chapters.summary: Ada and Teo open the strongroom on the third tide: gold, yes, but also documents proving the Meridian carried stolen relief funds — money meant for towns like theirs. Emotional beat: treasure turning to ash in the hands.

chapters.title: Junie Confesses
chapters.summary: Junie's POV: she admits she tipped off Crane weeks ago, needing money for her daughter's surgery; the sabotage wasn't hers, though — someone inside the crew is working for Crane. Emotional beat: betrayal confessed, forgiveness withheld but not refused.

chapters.title: The Mole
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV: deduction narrows the traitor to Teo, whose debts match payments in Crane's ledger that Ruth recognizes from her harbormaster records. Confrontation is deferred — they still need his diving skills. Emotional beat: trust maintained as strategy, not feeling.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide: Crane's Shadow
chapters.summary: Ada's POV: the Corvus fleet shadows them into the channel; a near-collision forces Ada to fly reconnaissance through a storm to map Crane's positions. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into fierce competence.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide: The Captain's Cabin
chapters.summary: Teo's POV, redemptive turn: diving past his safe limits, he recovers the captain's sealed orders — proof her father acted under authority, and that Crane's family fortune was built on the theft. Teo chooses the crew over Crane. Emotional beat: a man buying back his soul with blood.

chapters.title: Storm Hold
chapters.summary: Junie's POV: weather pins everyone ashore for two days; Ada and Junie finally reconcile over their father's letters, agreeing that truth matters more than a clean memory of him. Emotional beat: love rebuilt on honest ground.

chapters.title: Crane's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Crane's POV: he seizes Ruth's skiff as collateral and gives Ada until the sixth tide to hand over the documents, or the town loses its harbor charter — which he controls through the debt holders. Emotional beat: cold menace revealing the true stakes aren't gold but the community itself.

chapters.title: The Plan Nobody Likes
chapters.summary: Ada's POV: she proposes giving Crane the documents — copies — while broadcasting the originals on the marine band so every coastal town hears the truth before Crane can bury it. The crew votes, barely. Emotional beat: terror and resolve braided together.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide: The Wreck
chapters.summary: Climax, Ada's POV: all parties converge in the cave as the tide turns. Crane takes the bait documents, discovers the forgery, and tries to seal the crew inside; Teo collapses the passage behind them, trapping the gold forever and stranding Crane's claim. Emotional beat: everything risked at once.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Ada's POV aftermath: the broadcast goes out; coastal towns rally, Crane's financing collapses under exposure, and the debt holders withdraw rather than face the towns they'd be foreclosing on. Ada walks away from the cave empty-handed and lighter. Emotional beat: grief and release in the same breath.

chapters.title: Charter Restored
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV: the harbor charter survives, the town throws a grudging celebration, and Junie's daughter gets her surgery through a fund the towns build themselves from the story. Emotional beat: a community discovering it was the treasure all along.

chapters.title: Compass True
chapters.summary: Ada's POV coda: she repaints her floatplane, files her father's real record with the maritime board, and takes off into clear weather with the compass now pointing nowhere in particular — just north. Emotional beat: identity no longer defined by debt or inheritance, but by choice.
